liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (2 reviews): Followed the Promised Land opener with a Sugaree running over seventeen minutes; Reviewer calls it the best Sugaree they have heard [8][9]
- **Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Jerry's soloing here is singled out as hair-raising and seemingly improvised [9]
- **Friend of the Devil** (1 other source): A separate first-set audience source supplies the crowd noise and noodling leading into this song [3]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): The Scarlet>Fire pairing is described as ethereal [9]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 other source): A 22-second patch from John Brennan's audience tape fills a gap in the soundboard here [2]

## The recordings

- **gd77-10-16.sbd.lai.3350.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 158 min; rated 4.55/5 by 29 [1]. Said about its sound: Second-set Scarlet>Fire>Estimated sounds long and ethereal; Jerry's guitar tone seems unlike the rest of 1977, as if borrowed; Leads and interplay are percussive and driving; the recording separates each instrument clearly, even by 1977 standards [7][16]
- **gd1977-10-16.151787.sbd.patched.clugston.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 158 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1977-10-16.151786.aud.brennan.miller.clugston.flac2448**: audience recording; 19 songs; 159 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1977-10-16.151785.aud.brennan.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 19 songs; 159 min [4]

## Around the show

- Uploader recalls little of the night beyond hashish, but made the channel-jumping noise heard during a break on this audience tape [5]
- Rumored to be the last show where Jerry played the Travis Bean guitar onstage, per deadlists [6]
- The show fell on Bobby's 30th birthday [8]
- Reserved seats sold out quickly, so the reviewer and a friend settled for general admission tickets bought at the last minute [14]
- According to deadbase, this was the only time Terrapin Station went straight into Black Peter [6]
- Reviewer saw Jerry play the Travis Bean in Tampa just over a year later, the only other time they saw it [15]
- Reviewer says first-set playing is unusually inventive, with every song containing things the band hadn't done before [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd77-10-16.sbd.lai.3350.sbefail.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard source transferred via Mike Lai, with a chain running through MR, C and D to CD [1]
- **gd1977-10-16.151787.sbd.patched.clugston.flac16**: transferred by Scott Clugston; source: Master Soundboard Reels > Cassette > DAT > CDR [2]. Also: Patched version of the shnid 3350 soundboard, with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones [2]
- **gd1977-10-16.151786.aud.brennan.miller.clugston.flac2448**: taped by Unknown; tape supplied by John Brennan; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Analog Audience source (unknown equipment) > Reel to Reel @ 3ips > John Brennan's Cassettes [3]. Also: Audience recording and transfer by John Brennan, with Charlie Miller coordinating and Joe B. Jones helping on pitch correction; Described as the first complete audience source in general circulation; it has cuts in The Other One and Around & Around [3]
- **gd1977-10-16.151785.aud.brennan.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Unknown; tape supplied by John Brennan; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Analog Audience source (unknown equipment) > Reel to Reel @ 3ips > John Brennan's Cassettes [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Assembly Center - October 16, 1977](https://www.dead.net/show/october-16-1977) [19]
